description: NaYF₄ crystallizes in the trigonal P3 space group. There are three inequivalent Na sites. In the first Na site, Na is bonded in a 6-coordinate geometry to six F atoms. There are three shorter (2.25 Å) and three longer (2.63 Å) Na-F bond lengths. In the second Na site, Na is bonded in a 6-coordinate geometry to six F atoms. There are three shorter (2.27 Å) and three longer (2.54 Å) Na-F bond lengths. In the third Na site, Na is bonded in a 9-coordinate geometry to nine F atoms. There are six shorter (2.47 Å) and three longer (2.55 Å) Na-F bond lengths. There are three inequivalent Y sites. In the first Y site, Y is bonded in a 9-coordinate geometry to nine F atoms. There are a spread of Y-F bond distances ranging from 2.30-2.39 Å. In the second Y site, Y is bonded in a 9-coordinate geometry to nine F atoms. There are a spread of Y-F bond distances ranging from 2.30-2.39 Å. In the third Y site, Y is bonded in a 9-coordinate geometry to nine F atoms. There are six shorter (2.32 Å) and three longer (2.40 Å) Y-F bond lengths. There are four inequivalent F sites. In the first F site, F is bonded in a distorted trigonal non-coplanar geometry to three Y atoms. In the second F site, F is bonded to three Na and two Y atoms to form distorted FNa₃Y₂ square pyramids that share corners with two equivalent FNa₃Y₂ square pyramids, corners with six FNa₂Y₂ tetrahedra, edges with four equivalent FNa₃Y₂ square pyramids, and edges with six FNa₂Y₂ tetrahedra. In the third F site, F is bonded to two Na and two Y atoms to form FNa₂Y₂ tetrahedra that share corners with three equivalent FNa₃Y₂ square pyramids, corners with ten FNa₂Y₂ tetrahedra, edges with three equivalent FNa₃Y₂ square pyramids, and edges with two equivalent FNa₂Y₂ tetrahedra. In the fourth F site, F is bonded to two Na and two Y atoms to form FNa₂Y₂ tetrahedra that share corners with three equivalent FNa₃Y₂ square pyramids, corners with ten FNa₂Y₂ tetrahedra, edges with three equivalent FNa₃Y₂ square pyramids, and edges with two equivalent FNa₂Y₂ tetrahedra.
